grade.rationale: The template is feature-rich and generally readable, but it contains several concrete interaction and accessibility defects, including unintended form submission, an inert close affordance, inaccessible form controls, incomplete table semantics, and no distinguishable file-load failure state. Test coverage is unknown, and ESLint evidence was unavailable.

summary: The main rendering paths appear coherent, but several controls do not behave or announce themselves as their markup suggests. The most important fixes are to make every non-submit button explicit, expose load failures, label comment fields, and correct the interactive table and sorting semantics.

grade.rationale: Two buttons can implicitly submit an ancestor form, the tab close glyph is not actionable, and file-loading failures have no distinct rendered state.
Angular control-flow blocks and consistent naming make the template navigable, although large single-line interaction sections and repeated accessibility omissions increase maintenance risk.
Most states are clearly presented, but the inert close glyph and indistinguishable empty/error outcomes create misleading UI signals.
The template represents loading and empty states but provides no explicit failure state or recovery action for an unsuccessful file request.
Stable classes and attributes provide useful selectors, but implicit button behavior and overloaded virtualized row markup make interaction tests more brittle. No coverage evidence was supplied.
Comment inputs lack durable accessible names, sortable headers do not expose sort state, the tab pattern lacks expected keyboard metadata, and buttons are repurposed as table rows.

findings.title: Non-submit controls can submit an ancestor form
findings.description: The aspect tab and finding marker omit `type="button"`. HTML buttons default to submit buttons, so either control can unexpectedly submit a form that contains this component.
findings.recommendation: Add `type="button"` to both buttons and add a regression test that renders the editor inside a form and verifies that activating them does not submit it.

findings.title: Tab close affordance is inert and inaccessible
findings.description: The multiplication sign is styled and positioned like a tab close control but is only a span with no click or keyboard behavior and no accessible name. Users are given a familiar actionable affordance that cannot be activated.
findings.recommendation: If the tab is closable, replace the span with a `type="button"` control having an accessible name and a close handler. If it is decorative, remove it or hide it from assistive technology and avoid close-control styling.

findings.title: File-load failures are indistinguishable from having no file open
findings.description: The file view renders a loading message while loading and later falls through to `No file open`, but it contains no failure message or retry action. A rejected or failed request can therefore appear to the user as an intentional empty selection.
findings.recommendation: Expose the API error state in this template and render a descriptive alert with an appropriate retry action before falling back to the genuine no-selection state.

findings.title: Comment entry fields lack durable accessible names
findings.description: The reply input and new-comment textarea rely only on placeholder text. Placeholders disappear as users type and are not a reliable substitute for programmatically associated labels.
findings.recommendation: Give each field a visible `<label>` or an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` that identifies the thread or source line. Keep the placeholder only as optional input guidance.

findings.title: Table rows override button semantics
findings.description: Risk and folder entries are native buttons whose accessible role is replaced with `row`. This creates a hybrid control: assistive technology receives table-row semantics while the element is expected to behave as a button, so its action may not be announced consistently.
findings.recommendation: Use structural `role="row"` elements containing correctly scoped cells and place a real button or link inside the appropriate cell. Alternatively, use a semantic table or grid pattern with documented keyboard interaction.

findings.title: Sortable column headers do not expose their current sort direction
findings.description: The column headers visually append sort indicators, but none sets `aria-sort`. Screen-reader users cannot reliably determine which column controls the current order or whether it is ascending or descending.
findings.recommendation: Bind `aria-sort` on the active `columnheader` to `ascending` or `descending`, and set it to `none` or omit it for inactive columns. Test both table variants after changing sort direction.

findings.title: Review-aspect tabs lack complete tab interaction semantics
findings.description: The controls declare `tablist` and `tab` roles and expose selection, but they do not identify corresponding tab panels, manage a single tab stop, or show keyboard handling for moving between tabs. This does not implement the interaction users expect from an ARIA tab interface.
findings.recommendation: Implement the complete tabs pattern: associate each tab with its panel using IDs and `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby`, use roving `tabindex`, and support arrow-key navigation. If that behavior is not intended, present the controls as an ordinary labelled button group instead of tabs.
